By: Sasha Schwendenwein | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The balaclava rapist has been arrested. Carte Blanche has the exclusive with the police and speaks to one of the victims.

Summary:
In April Carte Blanche brought you the story of the Alexandra Balaclava Rapist, where the modus operandi was the same for over 100 reported cases at the Alexandra police station.
One victim was “Lindiwe,” her and her boyfriend “Thabo” were taken 2 years ago. The couple were forced into the Jukskei rivers east bank graveyard at gun point. Tabo was then compelled to rape Lindiwe. Tabo’s face was then covered and the Lindiwe was raped for a second time. Sometimes there was more than one man, and at the beginning of this year there was also more than one couple taken at the same time.

LINK: AT THE TIME OF OUR STORY THERE WERE 112 REPORTED CASES AT THIS POLICE STATION, AND OVER 200 VICTIMS. THE CASES ARE SUSPECTED TO HAVE BEGUN 10 YEARS AGO IN 2005, AND SOME VICTIMS WERE AS YOUNG AS 14 YEARS OLD. (OUTSIDE ALEXANDRA POLICE STATION)

WHEN WE WENT TO THE POLICE TO ASK QUESTIONS IN OUR ORIGINAL STORY THEY DECLINED THE INTERVIEW. HOWEVER, WE ARE HERE AT POLICE CENTRAL AND THEY HAVE FINALLY MADE A BERAK IN THE CASE. Article:
http://www.wits.ac.za/newsroom/newsitems/201506/26675/news_item_26675.html - LISA VETTEN - Please read – latest rape stats
Official statistics don't tell the full story
While the official police statistics reflect decreases in sexual offences, other sources say something very different.
Figures released by the South African Police Service earlier this year show that crimes against children decreased by more than 3000 between 2012-13 and 2013-14. Conviction rates increased to 75% and more than 1832 life sentences were secured for perpetrators of these crimes. The numbers echoed the 2014 crime statistics, which showed that rape had declined by 6.2% between 2008-09 and 2013-14.
Various media outlets have, in the past, reported that Interpol has crowned South Africa the rape capital of the world at least twice. The BBC alleges that South African women are more likely to be raped than learn to read. Another British newspaper asserts that up to 40% of women suffer this fate in their lifetimes. The "Blow the Whistle" campaign from a local non-government organisation claims that one in three South African women will experience rape.
While these statistics may be alarming, none are derived from credible research. And they do not assist the public to understand the problem around violence against women and children. And neither of these sets of numbers capture the rapes that are never brought to the police's attention.
A more accurate picture of the extent of sexual violence in the country is emerging from credible bodies such as the Medical Research Council, as well as research by not-for-profit organisations.
In 2002, drawing on data from the 1997 national South African Demographic and Health Survey, the Medical Research Council found that only one in seven women who had been raped reported the matter to police.
Research conducted 12 years after the 1997 survey suggests that under-reporting persists. Interviews conducted in the Gauteng province in 2009 showed that one in 12 women in the province had been raped that year, but only one of every 13 women raped by someone who was not their partner reported the matter. The number was even more startling for women who had been raped by their partner. Only one in 25 reported this to police.
The same study was undertaken in KwaZulu-Natal and Limpopo. In KwaZulu-Natal, one in seven women who had experienced rape reported the matter while one of every six women raped by non-partners in Limpopo informed the police.

5. Been on Nhleko’s desk since March – has this been signed yet? If not, why?
6. Tell me about the DNA act?
7. Explain the DNA police database?
8. During the making of this document it was discovered that there have been over “1000 unsolved rape series” identified. What is an unsolved rape series?
9. 1000 SERIAL RAPISTS OUT THERE?
10. According to the policy document, out of every 20 attacks maybe 5 will be have DNA that can be linked due to loss of evidence – what are you doing to solve this problem?

Press Release:


Balaclava Rapist Nabbed
For years, members of the Alexandra community have stood by, helpless and terrified, as cases of rape and assault at the hands of the so-called Balaclava serial rapist have mounted - reaching a staggering 112 reported incidents. Four months after a Carte Blanche investigation exposed this horror, several suspects have finally been arrested and their DNA matched to the crimes reported. Carte Blanche shares details of this intricate investigation, that is far from over.


Script:


The so-called Balaclava serial rapist has terrorised Alexandra township residents for a decade, robbing couples at gunpoint and raping multiple women. But is there only one balaclava rapist? In April this year Carte Blanche investigated reports that there were over 100 rape cases at the Alexandra police station all linked to a perpetrator who wore a balaclava. But recent arrests suggest that Alexandra is plagued by up to 3 groups of serial rapists who mask themselves with balaclavas. In April, our report focused on one armed criminal group who forced multiple couples into a nearby cemetery. Their cell phones were often taken. Simphiwe and her boyfriend were two such victims.
Simphiwe: He was wearing a balacava. He first compelled Simphiwe’s boyfriend to rape her.
Simphiwe: “He pointed a gun on us and said, “you’re doing it here while im watching you.”
He then covered Simphiwe’s boyfriends face.
Simphiwe: “That’s when he raped me. He got me when I was a virgin.”
LINK: AT THE TIME OF OUR STORY THERE WERE OVER 112 REPORTED CASES AT THIS POLICE STATION, THE CASES WENT BACK 10 YEARS, AND SOME OF THE VICTIMS WERE AS YOUNG AS 14 YEARS OLD.
The rapes occurred within the 3-kilometer radius of the Alexandra Jukskei Park and cemetery.
LINK: VICTIMS TOLD US THAT WHEN THEY WENT TO THE ALEXANDER POLICE STATION TO REPORT THE RAPES, THEY WERE LAUGHED AT AND TOLD THEY WERE ONE OF MANY VICTIMS. THE POLICE THREATENED TO INTERDICT THE STORY TO PREVENT IT FROM BEING BROADCAST AND DECLINED ALL INTERVIEWS BECAUSE THEY DID NOT WANT TO HARM THE INVESTIGATION. IT’S BEEN FOUR MONTHS AND THEY ARE NOW WILLING TO SIT DOWN AND GIVE US INFORMATION.
There are now two suspects in custody. Colonel Lungelo Dlamini, SAPS Gauteng provincial spokesperson said a task team captured the first suspect using geo-location technology through which they traced one of the victim’s cell phones.
Dlamini: During arrest, the police found him in possession of an unlicensed firearm.”
Whilst in custody, the suspect’s DNA was sent for testing and compared against the police DNA database. The results were fast-tracked.
Dlamini: “There are 10 cases that he has been linked to, but there are more than 45 victims that are being investigated at this stage.”
Dlamini said that because the balaclava rapist targets couples the number of possible victims stands at double that – at 90.
Dlamini: “The other suspect, also who has been arrested, was pointed out by one of the witnesses, he’s still in prison, but we are still also waiting for the DNA results.”
LINK: IT HAS NOT BEEN ESTABLISHED WHICH OF THE TWO MEN IS THE MAIN BALACLAVA RAPIST, ONE OF THE SUSPECTS IS APPEARING IN COURT RIGHT NOW.
SIJA ROBIN MUSLIM MABITSELA HAS BEEN CHARGED WITH ONE COUNT OF RAPE. THE POLICE AWAIT DNA RESULTS ON THAT CASE. HE APPLIED FOR BAIL, AND THE CASE HAS BEEN POSTPONED to AUGUST 21st. THE SECOND suspect, AMSEKA JOSIAS MKANSI HAS BEEN CHARGED WITH 10 COUNTS OF RAPE AND WILL APPEAR BEFORE COURT ON SEPTEMBER 23rd.
Though 112 rape cases have possibly been linked to the Balaclava rapist less than half have been linked to the two arrested suspects.
Dlamini: “We haven’t linked all these cases to these two people, because we believe there might be more than two groups that have been operating there in Alexandra.”
Devi: So there are two possibly three groups operating, and you’ve arrested two?
Dlamini: “We’ve got 3 suspects that have been linked to the rapes in Alexandra, but those suspects are also linked to several cases in other areas like murder, rape, attempted murder and robbery.”
These three suspects also wore balaclavas and are possibly connected to 33 more cases. But, their modus operandi is different.
Dlamini: “They they were promising the women some jobs, once they get the victim, they will take the victim to the graveyard, and they rape them.”
This week one of the three suspects appeared in the Kagiso Magistrate’s Court.
Brian Thabiso Eric pleaded guilty to kidnapping, rape and murder charge. He was denied bail and will appear in court tomorrow. The other two of the three suspects remain in police custody.
And, in addition to the two groups whose members have been arrested, Dlamini said there is a suspected third group STILL operating in Alex.
Dlamini: “We believe there are still suspects who are out there, who are also committing crimes, using balaclavas.”
Devi: So this is bigger than we ever imagined?
Dlamini: “There might be other people who are also responsible for the rapes.”
Devi: Because this shows the balaclava rapist was not a myth?
Dlamini: “He was real.”
It’s been two years since Simphiwe and her boyfriend were attacked.
Devi: How have you been since we last spoke?
Simpiwe: “I’ve been doing great, I knew that one of the good days, I might get the good news, as I did now.”
A burning question remains. Why did it take the police ten years to make arrests? It is clear that Carte Blanche’s April investigation put pressure on the Task Team, and was the catalyst to arrests being made. It was only then that suspect DNA became available.
Lisa: “The longer you are unaware that somebody is operating, the more opportunity you give them to accumulate victims and unfortunately for the victim pile to pile up.”
Lisa Vetten is with the Wits Institute for social and economic research. She assisted the police in drafting two rape policies that were signed into action two weeks ago. They will reduce barriers to reporting sexual offences and streamline management of serial-rape and murder investigations.
Lisa: “This policy is an attempt to say the minute a serial is identified, there has to be a task team formed immediately, all information, all dockets must be shared and you have a team.”
In Gauteng the Medical Research Council found that 1 in 13 women don’t report rape. Even more shocking was another truth that arose during Lisa’s discussions with police officers.
LINK: ACCORDING TO THE POLICE THERE ARE OVER 1000 SERIAL RAPISTS PROWLING OUR STREETS. THIS STAGGERING FIGURE WAS ESTABLISHED THROUGH DNA EVIDENCE MATCHED ON THE POLICE’S DATABASE, BUT, WE’RE TALKING ABOUT SERIAL RAPISTS, WHICH MEANS THAT FOR EVERY SINGLE DNA MATCH THERE ARE A MINIMUM OF AT LEAST TWO OPEN RAPE CASES, WHERE THE SUSPECTS HAVE NOT BEEN APPREHENDED.
Lisa: “Serial rape is the one kind of crime the police can prevent, if we can take 1000 men out of the equation we would really do quite a significant job of reducing rape in South Africa.”
Devi: Are you relieved?
Dlamini: “I will be relieved once everybody who was involved in those criminal activities has been brought into custody.”
On Friday evening the police and members of the Alexandra community policing forum took to the streets. Elizabeth Mokoena, manager of the Alexandra Victims Unit – who appeared in our April story was there. She has been fundamental to raising awareness of the balaclava rapist crimes in Alex.

Singing

In a women’s month campaign called “ Take back the night,” the women of Alexandra visited rape hotspots. Victims of the balaclava rapists were encouraged to come forward by Community Safety MEC Sizakele Nkosi Malobane, who had strong words for remaining members of the Balaclava gangs.

“I promise you, if people come to us and report these cases, we will make sure, before the end of the year, all those people will be standing trial.”
Devi: Is there anything you’d like to say to other victims?
Simphiwe: “You’re not the only one, is that they must stay strong, and believe that one day this man will pay for what he did.”
For now the third group of balaclava-wearing criminals remains at large.

Simphiwe: “He pointed a gun on us and said, “you’re doing it here while im watching you.” He then covered Simphiwe’s boyfriends face. Simphiwe: “That’s when he raped me. He got me when I was a virgin.” LINK: AT THE TIME OF OUR STORY THERE WERE OVER 112 REPORTED CASES AT THIS POLICE STATION, THE CASES WENT BACK 10 YEARS, AND SOME OF THE VICTIMS WERE AS YOUNG AS 14 YEARS OLD. The rapes occurred within the 3-kilometer radius of the Alexandra Jukskei Park and cemetery. LINK: VICTIMS TOLD US THAT WHEN THEY WENT TO THE ALEXANDER POLICE STATION TO REPORT THE RAPES, THEY WERE LAUGHED AT AND TOLD THEY WERE ONE OF MANY VICTIMS. THE POLICE THREATENED TO INTERDICT THE STORY TO PREVENT IT FROM BEING BROADCAST AND DECLINED ALL INTERVIEWS BECAUSE THEY DID NOT WANT TO HARM THE INVESTIGATION. IT’S BEEN FOUR MONTHS AND THEY ARE NOW WILLING TO SIT DOWN AND GIVE US INFORMATION. There are now two suspects in custody. Colonel Lungelo Dlamini, SAPS Gauteng provincial spokesperson said a task team captured the first suspect using geo-location technology through which they traced one of the victim’s cell phones. Dlamini: During arrest, the police found him in possession of an unlicensed firearm.” Whilst in custody, the suspect’s DNA was sent for testing and compared against the police DNA database. The results were fast-tracked. Dlamini: “There are 10 cases that he has been linked to, but there are more than 45 victims that are being investigated at this stage.” Dlamini said that because the balaclava rapist targets couples the number of possible victims stands at double that – at 90. Dlamini: “The other suspect, also who has been arrested, was pointed out by one of the witnesses, he’s still in prison, but we are still also waiting for the DNA results.” LINK: IT HAS NOT BEEN ESTABLISHED WHICH OF THE TWO MEN IS THE MAIN BALACLAVA RAPIST, ONE OF THE SUSPECTS IS APPEARING IN COURT RIGHT NOW. SIJA ROBIN MUSLIM MABITSELA HAS BEEN CHARGED WITH ONE COUNT OF RAPE. THE POLICE AWAIT DNA RESULTS ON THAT CASE. HE APPLIED FOR BAIL, AND THE CASE HAS BEEN POSTPONED to AUGUST 21st. THE SECOND suspect, AMSEKA JOSIAS MKANSI HAS BEEN CHARGED WITH 10 COUNTS OF RAPE AND WILL APPEAR BEFORE COURT ON SEPTEMBER 23rd. Though 112 rape cases have possibly been linked to the Balaclava rapist less than half have been linked to the two arrested suspects. Dlamini: “We haven’t linked all these cases to these two people, because we believe there might be more than two groups that have been operating there in Alexandra.” Devi: So there are two possibly three groups operating, and you’ve arrested two? Dlamini: “We’ve got 3 suspects that have been linked to the rapes in Alexandra, but those suspects are also linked to several cases in other areas like murder, rape, attempted murder and robbery.” These three suspects also wore balaclavas and are possibly connected to 33 more cases. But, their modus operandi is different. Dlamini: “They they were promising the women some jobs, once they get the victim, they will take the victim to the graveyard, and they rape them.” This week one of the three suspects appeared in the Kagiso Magistrate’s Court. Brian Thabiso Eric pleaded guilty to kidnapping, rape and murder charge. He was denied bail and will appear in court tomorrow. The other two of the three suspects remain in police custody. And, in addition to the two groups whose members have been arrested, Dlamini said there is a suspected third group STILL operating in Alex. Dlamini: “We believe there are still suspects who are out there, who are also committing crimes, using balaclavas.” Devi: So this is bigger than we ever imagined? Dlamini: “There might be other people who are also responsible for the rapes.” Devi: Because this shows the balaclava rapist was not a myth? Dlamini: “He was real.” It’s been two years since Simphiwe and her boyfriend were attacked. Devi: How have you been since we last spoke? Simpiwe: “I’ve been doing great, I knew that one of the good days, I might get the good news, as I did now.” A burning question remains. Why did it take the police ten years to make arrests? It is clear that Carte Blanche’s April investigation put pressure on the Task Team, and was the catalyst to arrests being made. It was only then that suspect DNA became available. Lisa: “The longer you are unaware that somebody is operating, the more opportunity you give them to accumulate victims and unfortunately for the victim pile to pile up.” Lisa Vetten is with the Wits Institute for social and economic research. She assisted the police in drafting two rape policies that were signed into action two weeks ago. They will reduce barriers to reporting sexual offences and streamline management of serial-rape and murder investigations. Lisa: “This policy is an attempt to say the minute a serial is identified, there has to be a task team formed immediately, all information, all dockets must be shared and you have a team.” In Gauteng the Medical Research Council found that 1 in 13 women don’t report rape. Even more shocking was another truth that arose during Lisa’s discussions with police officers. LINK: ACCORDING TO THE POLICE THERE ARE OVER 1000 SERIAL RAPISTS PROWLING OUR STREETS. THIS STAGGERING FIGURE WAS ESTABLISHED THROUGH DNA EVIDENCE MATCHED ON THE POLICE’S DATABASE, BUT, WE’RE TALKING ABOUT SERIAL RAPISTS, WHICH MEANS THAT FOR EVERY SINGLE DNA MATCH THERE ARE A MINIMUM OF AT LEAST TWO OPEN RAPE CASES, WHERE THE SUSPECTS HAVE NOT BEEN APPREHENDED. Lisa: “Serial rape is the one kind of crime the police can prevent, if we can take 1000 men out of the equation we would really do quite a significant job of reducing rape in South Africa.” Devi: Are you relieved? Dlamini: “I will be relieved once everybody who was involved in those criminal activities has been brought into custody.” On Friday evening the police and members of the Alexandra community policing forum took to the streets. Elizabeth Mokoena, manager of the Alexandra Victims Unit – who appeared in our April story was there. She has been fundamental to raising awareness of the balaclava rapist crimes in Alex. Singing In a women’s month campaign called “ Take back the night,” the women of Alexandra visited rape hotspots. Victims of the balaclava rapists were encouraged to come forward by Community Safety MEC Sizakele Nkosi Malobane, who had strong words for remaining members of the Balaclava gangs. “I promise you, if people come to us and report these cases, we will make sure, before the end of the year, all those people will be standing trial.” Devi: Is there anything you’d like to say to other victims? Simphiwe: “You’re not the only one, is that they must stay strong, and believe that one day this man will pay for what he did.” For now the third group of balaclava-wearing criminals remains at large. Article: http://www.wits.ac.za/newsroom/newsitems/201506/26675/news_item_26675.html - LISA VETTEN - Please read – latest rape stats Official statistics don't tell the full story While the official police statistics reflect decreases in sexual offences, other sources say something very different. Figures released by the South African Police Service earlier this year show that crimes against children decreased by more than 3000 between 2012-13 and 2013-14. Conviction rates increased to 75% and more than 1832 life sentences were secured for perpetrators of these crimes. The numbers echoed the 2014 crime statistics, which showed that rape had declined by 6.2% between 2008-09 and 2013-14. Various media outlets have, in the past, reported that Interpol has crowned South Africa the rape capital of the world at least twice. The BBC alleges that South African women are more likely to be raped than learn to read. Another British newspaper asserts that up to 40% of women suffer this fate in their lifetimes. The "Blow the Whistle" campaign from a local non-government organisation claims that one in three South African women will experience rape. While these statistics may be alarming, none are derived from credible research. And they do not assist the public to understand the problem around violence against women and children. And neither of these sets of numbers capture the rapes that are never brought to the police's attention. A more accurate picture of the extent of sexual violence in the country is emerging from credible bodies such as the Medical Research Council, as well as research by not-for-profit organisations. In 2002, drawing on data from the 1997 national South African Demographic and Health Survey, the Medical Research Council found that only one in seven women who had been raped reported the matter to police. Research conducted 12 years after the 1997 survey suggests that under-reporting persists. Interviews conducted in the Gauteng province in 2009 showed that one in 12 women in the province had been raped that year, but only one of every 13 women raped by someone who was not their partner reported the matter. The number was even more startling for women who had been raped by their partner. Only one in 25 reported this to police. The same study was undertaken in KwaZulu-Natal and Limpopo. In KwaZulu-Natal, one in seven women who had experienced rape reported the matter while one of every six women raped by non-partners in Limpopo informed the police. QUESTIONS FOR POLICE: 1.
